notes: Lead source: self-serve signup (quickstart) — used free trial credits, small engineering team.
Primary workload: chat for customer support + document search; avg session ~4 turns, common prompts include 600-900 token doc snippets.
Reported problem: intermittent latency spikes and client-side timeouts. Frontend sees axios timeouts ~2s frequently during peak; perceived as 'service instability'.
Observed perf (baseline): median response latency ~350ms for single-turn prompts in us-west-2; 95th percentile ~1.2s in us-east-1 during 9-11am PST (customer telemetry).
Customer quote: 'Most of our errors are timeouts from the browser, not 500s.' — Lead dev.
Asked: how to reduce tail latency and what immediate tuning steps we recommend for hosted API (public cloud).
Recommended quick wins provided on call:
- Pick region close to users: recommend us-west-2 for west-coast customers; eu-west-1 for EU users. Call out region param at API layer to avoid cross-region hops.
- Increase client HTTP timeout: many frontends use 2s default. Recommend 8000ms conservative setting for initial response, or implement streaming to surface tokens earlier.
- Enable streaming: reduces perceived latency; for multi-turn chat, stream first tokens to the client and fetch rest in background.

- Trim prompt context: move long doc retrieval to on-demand embeddings + reranking; cap max_prompt_tokens and truncate long system messages; prefer sending a synthesized context (200-400 tokens) rather than raw full docs.
- Use model selection to balance cost vs latency: small/quantized variants for embeddings and reranking; reserve larger models only for high-complexity responses.
- Client-side retry/backoff: switch to exponential backoff for transient tail spikes; avoid aggressive parallel retries that amplify load.
Implementation notes we agreed to share:
- Example headers: set X-Request-Timeout-ms=8000 and use chunked transfer for streaming responses.
- Server config: nginx proxy timeout ≧10s for initial request path, keepalive for streaming connections.
